title: "F-eqv — Equivocal, adaptively secure commitment"
status: "Canonical"
layer: 4
definition: "Not yet written"
---

*F-eqv* (Equivocal, adaptively secure commitment) is part of *Commitments and Proofs* in the UC functionality encyclopedia. Status: a canonical, well-established UC functionality.

Equivocability (in Beaver's sense) is a protocol-level technique — not a distinct ideal functionality — for UC-realizing *F-COM*/*F-MCOM* under adaptive corruption; see Canetti and Fischlin's erasure-based construction.

*References:*

- Canetti and Fischlin. [*Universally composable commitments*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2001/055). In Advances in Cryptology – CRYPTO 2001, volume 2139 of LNCS, pages 19–40, 2001.
- Beaver. [*Adaptive zero-knowledge and computational equivocation*](https://doi.org/10.1145/237814.238014). In 28th ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC), 1996.
